_source.description: Major global niobium (columbium) mining and production sites
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Niobium (Columbium) chapter (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-niobium.pdf); USGS Mineral Resources Data System (MRDS) (https://mrdata.usgs.gov/mrds/); CBMM corporate publications (https://cbmm.com/); CMOC Group annual reports (SEHK: 3993); Anglo American plc Annual Report 2023 (LSE: AAL); Magris Resources corporate publications; NioBay Metals Inc (TSXV: NBY) filings; Cradle Resources (ASX: CXX) project reports; Globe Metals & Mining (ASX: GBE) technical reports; Niobec mine data from Quebec mining records (MERN); S&P Global Market Intelligence mine profiles
_source.license: USGS: public domain; company data: fair use summary
_source.notes: Niobium production is extremely concentrated — Brazil (~90% via CBMM Araxa and CMOC/Anglo American operations) and Canada (~10% via Niobec). All capacity figures in niobium content (ferroniobium equivalent) tonnes per annum. Coordinates from USGS MRDS, company technical reports, and satellite verification. Many sites outside Brazil/Canada are exploration or development stage with no current production.

_coverage.global_production_source: USGS MCS 2024 — estimated 78,000 tonnes Nb content
_coverage.known_gaps: Small artisanal coltan operations in DRC/Rwanda that produce minor Nb by-product; Chinese Nb recovery from slag is not site-specific

sites.name: Araxa (CBMM)
sites.operator: CBMM (Companhia Brasileira de Metalurgia e Mineracao)
sites.notes: World's largest niobium mine — supplies ~70% of global Nb; pyrochlore carbonatite complex in Minas Gerais; CBMM is the world's dominant FeNb producer

sites.name: Catalao (Boa Vista)
sites.ownership: CMOC Group (100%, acquired from Anglo American 2016)
sites.notes: Second-largest Nb mine globally; Boa Vista carbonatite complex in Goias state; integrated FeNb production; formerly Anglo American Niobras

sites.name: Catalao II (Anglo American)
sites.notes: Separate carbonatite body adjacent to CMOC's Boa Vista; Anglo American retained this asset after selling Niobras to CMOC

sites.name: Araxa (CMOC Phosphate Complex)
sites.notes: Nb recovered as by-product from CMOC's phosphate operations adjacent to CBMM; separate from Catalao

sites.name: Seis Lagos
sites.operator: CPRM (Geological Survey of Brazil) / Government reserve
sites.notes: Potentially world's largest Nb deposit; Sao Gabriel da Cachoeira, Amazonas state; located in indigenous territory (Yanomami); remote location in Amazon; held as strategic reserve

sites.name: Morro dos Seis Lagos
sites.notes: Northern portion of the Seis Lagos complex; enormous inferred resource; environmental and indigenous territory constraints

sites.name: Morro do Padre
sites.notes: Alto Paranaiba carbonatite province, Goias; part of the same alkaline-carbonatite belt as Araxa and Catalao; exploration stage

sites.name: Niobec
sites.ownership: Magris Resources (100%, acquired from IAMGOLD 2015); CMOC attempted acquisition withdrawn
sites.notes: Only underground niobium mine in the world; Saint-Honore carbonatite complex, Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean, Quebec; North America's sole Nb producer

sites.name: Oka Complex
sites.notes: James Bay Niobium Project; Oka carbonatite complex near Montreal; PEA completed; proximity to infrastructure but near residential areas

sites.name: Aley
sites.notes: Large carbonatite body in northern British Columbia; PEA completed; remote location in Rocky Mountain foothills

sites.name: Elk Creek
sites.notes: Only significant Nb deposit in the US; southeastern Nebraska; USDA conditional loan commitment; would be first primary Nb mine in US history

sites.name: Tomtor
sites.notes: Extremely high-grade Nb-REE deposit in Yakutia, Siberia; Buranny ore body; extreme Arctic conditions; logistics via Lena River; world-class grades but remote

sites.name: Lueshe
sites.notes: Former producer in North Kivu; operations suspended due to security situation; pyrochlore concentrate was exported to processing facilities

sites.name: Panda Hill
sites.ownership: Cradle Resources (50%), Tanzania government (16% free-carried interest)
sites.notes: Carbonatite complex near Mbeya; DFS completed 2016; FeNb production targeted; one of few advanced non-Brazil/Canada Nb projects

sites.name: Songwe Hill
sites.notes: Primarily a REE project in Phalombe District; Nb as minor by-product from carbonatite; PFS completed

sites.name: Kanyika
sites.notes: Multi-commodity project in Mzimba District, northern Malawi; PFS completed; planned FeNb production; uranium by-product adds regulatory complexity

sites.name: Bonga
sites.notes: Longonjo REE project, Huambo Province; Nb as potential by-product; DFS completed; Saltend (UK) processing hub planned

sites.name: Sukulu
sites.notes: Sukulu Hills carbonatite complex near Tororo; primarily phosphate with Nb-REE by-products; Chinese-funded development

sites.name: Ghurayyah
sites.notes: Large rare-metal granite deposit in Hejaz region; contains Nb-Ta-REE mineralization; PFS stage; part of Saudi Vision 2030 mining diversification

sites.name: Motzfeldt
sites.notes: Alkaline syenite complex in southern Greenland; early-stage exploration; Arctic conditions limit access
